174.subject: Botany
174.text:
Assertion : Mitochondria and chloroplasts are semi-autonomous organelles.
Reason : They are formed by division of preexisting organelles as well as contain DNA but lack protein synthesizing machinery.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
174.sol: Mitochondria and chloroplasts both are double membrane organelles. They are semi autonomous as both their structure and functions are partially controlled by nucleus of the cell and partially themselves. Both possess their own DNA and arises from pre-existing cells. Synthesis of many amino acids occurs in mitochondria. The first formed amino acids are glutamic acid and aspartic acid. Plastid also manufacture some of its own proteins, enzymes and other chemicals because of the presence of $70 \mathrm{~s}$ ribosomes which can help translate the coded information contained in mRNAs transcribed over chloroplast DNA.

2089.text: In humans at the end of first meiotic division, the male germ cells differentiate into the
2089.sol: At sexual maturity, the undifferentiated primordial germ cells divide several times by mitosis to produce a large number of spermatogonia. Each spermatogonium then actively grows to a larger primary spermatocyte. Each primary spermatocyte undergoes two successive divisions, called maturation divisions. The first maturation division is reductional or meiotic. Hence, the primary spermatocyte divides into the haploid daughter cells called secondary spermatocytes.

2843.text: The hybridization of $Se$ in ${SeF}_{4}$ and its geometry respectively are
2843.sol:
Selenium has the six unpaired electron in outermost shell for bonding. After that four electrons formed the bonding with the fluorine atoms and one lone pair present on the selenium. It has the see-saw shape geometry because on the repulsion due to lone pair. It has the four bond pair and one lone pair with steric number five. It has the hybridization of ${sp}^{3}d$.

Hence, the hybridization of $Se$ in ${SeF}_{4}$ and its geometry respectively are ${sp}^{3}d$, see-saw shaped.

5028.sol:
Solvay process is used in the manufacture of sodium carbonate, $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3$. This process involves following reactions.
$\begin{aligned}& \mathrm{NH}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{CO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{HCO}_3 \\& \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{HCO}_3+\mathrm{NaCl} \longrightarrow \mathrm{NaHCO}_3+\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl} \\& \hline \mathrm{NH}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{CO}_2+\mathrm{NaCl} \longrightarrow \mathrm{NaHCO}_3 \\&+\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}
\end{aligned}$
The sodium bicarbonate obtained on heating gives sodium carbonate.
$\mathrm{NaHCO}_3 \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{CO}_2$
Note: This process cannot be used in the manufacture of potassium carbonate as potassium bicarbonate is soluble in the solution of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$ and KCl.

At $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{dx}^2}=\left(\frac{1}{39}\right) \frac{1}{\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4}\right)^4} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{dx}^2}=\left(\frac{1}{39}\right) \times \frac{1}{\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2 \times 2}\right)}=\frac{4 \sqrt{2}}{39}\end{aligned}$

8831.subject: Mathematics
8831.text: If $f: A \to B$ and $g: B \to C$ are two functions such that $gof: A \to C$ is a bijection, then which one of the following is always true?
options: $f$ is an injection and $g$ is a surjection
$f$ is a surjection and $g$ is an injection
$f$ is a bijection but $g$ is not a bijection
8831.sol:
Given:

$f: A \to B$ and $g: B \to C$

And, $gof: A \to C$ is a bijection.

Let $x, y \in A$ such that $f \left(x\right) = f \left(y\right)$.

Then,

$f \left(x\right) = f \left(y\right)$

$⇒ g \left(f \left(x\right)\right) = g \left(f\left(y\right)\right)$

$⇒ gof \left(x\right) = gof \left(y\right)$

$⇒ x = y; \left[∵ gof: A \to $ C$\text{is one-one}\right]

Hence, $ f $\left(x\right)$ is an injection.

Now,

Let $z$ be an arbitrary element of $C$.

Since, $gof: A \to C$ is onto.

Therefore, there exists $x \in A$ such that

$gof\left(x\right) = z$

$⇒ g\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = z$

$⇒ g\left(y\right) = z$ where $y = f\left(x\right) \in B$.

Thus, for all $z \in C$ there exists $y = f\left(x\right) \in B$ such that $g\left(y\right) = z$.

Hence, $g: B \to C$& is surjection.

$$

15796.text: A car moving with a certain velocity, jumps from an inclined plane placed at one bank of a river and reaches the other bank by attained a maximum height of \(80 $\mathrm{ m}$\). If the same car, moving with the same velocity jumps from another inclined plane having different angle of inclination and reaches the same point on the other bank by attaining maximum height of \(45 $\mathrm{ m}$\), then the width of the river is
15796.sol:
Given, the maximum height reached by the car jumps from an inclined plane placed at one back of river is \(H_1=80 $\mathrm{ m}$\)
The second maximum height reached by car jumps from another inclined plane placed at other bank is \(\mathrm{H}}_{2}=45  \mathrm{ m}\)
Let the certain velocity of moving car \(=u\)
Let the inclination angle in first jump \(=\boldsymbol{\theta}_1\)
Let the inclination angle in second jump \(=\theta_2\)
We know that,
the maximum height of projectile given as
\(H=\frac{u^2 \sin \theta}{2 g}\)
For first case,
\(\begin{aligned}
& H_1=\frac{u^2 \sin ^2 \theta_1}{2 g}\\
& 80=\frac{u^2}{2 g} \sin ^2 \theta_1 \quad \ldots (i)
\end{aligned}\)
Similarly, for second case, \(H_2=\frac{u^2}{2 g} \sin ^2 \theta_2\)...(ii)
Dividing Eqs. (i) by (ii), we get
\(\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad \frac{H_1}{H_2}& =\frac{\frac{u^2}{2 g} \sin ^2 \theta_1}{\frac{u^2}{2 g} \sin ^2 \theta_2}\\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{80}{45}& =\frac{\sin ^2 \theta_1}{\sin ^2 \theta_2}\\
\frac{\sin \theta_1}{\sin \theta_2}& =\frac{4}{3}\\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\sin \theta_1}{\sin \theta_2}& =\frac{\frac{4}{3}}{5}
\end{aligned}\)
Now, \(\sin \theta_1=\frac{4}{5}\) or \(\theta_1=\sin ^{-1}$\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)=$53^{{}^{\circ}}\)
\(\therefore \quad \sin \theta_2=\frac{3}{5}\)
or \(\quad \theta_2=\sin ^{-1}$\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)=$37^{{}^{\circ}}\)...(iv)
Now, from Eq. (i), we get
\(\begin{aligned}
& 80=$\left(\frac{u^2}{g}\right)\left(\frac{\sin ^2 53}{2}\right)\text{ or }80=\left(\frac{u^2}{g}\right)\left[\frac{  \left(\frac{4}{5}\right)$^$2$}{2}\right]\\
 $\frac{u^2}{g}=\frac{80 \times 25 \times 2}{16}$\\
 $\frac{u^2}{g}=$250 \quad \ldots (v)
\end{aligned}\)
\(\therefore\) Width of the river given as
\(\begin{aligned}
 $d=\$left(\frac{u^2}{g}\right) \sin$2 \theta\\
 $$d=\frac{u^2}{g}\left(2 \sin \theta_1 \cos \theta_1\right) \\
& \quad(\because \sin 2 $\theta=$2 \sin $\theta \cos \theta \text{ and consider }\\
& \left.\qquad \theta=\theta_$1 $\text{ for first case }\right)
\end{aligned}\)
From Eqs. (v) and (iii), we get
\(\begin{aligned}
& \therefore d=250 \times2 \times \frac{4}{5} \times \frac{3}{5} \quad\left[\therefore \sin \t$theta_1=\frac{4}{5} \text{ then } \cos \t$theta_1=\frac{3}{5}\right]\\
& d=20 \times2 \times4 \times3=240  \mathrm{ m}\\
& d=240 \mathrm{ m}
\end{aligned}$\)
Hence, the width of the river is \(240 $\mathrm{ m}$\).

& T_1=27^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}=300 \mathrm{ K}\\

& =2^{2+\frac{5}{2}}=2^{\frac{9}{2}}

19994.subject: Chemistry
19994.text:
Match the coordination compounds in Column I having the given type of hybridisation of $\mathrm{M}^{\mathrm{n}+}$ ion and magnetic moment as given in Column II.
$Coordination compounds.\text{ Hybridisation \Magnetic nature. }ANi(CO)_4Psp^3, \quad \mu=5.92 BMB{\left[Ni(CN)_4\right]^{2-}}Qsp^3, \quad \mu=2.84 BMC{\left[Ni(Cl)_4\right]^{2-}}Rsp^3, \quad \mu=0D{[MnBr]^{2-}}Sdsp^2, \quad \mu=0$
19994.sol:
For $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$, the oxidation state of Ni is 0. The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^8 4s^2$. Since CO is a strong field ligand, it causes pairing of electrons, leading to $sp^3$ hybridization. All electrons are paired, so $\mu = 0$. This matches R.

For $[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}$, the oxidation state of Ni is +2. The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^8$. CN$^-$ is a strong field ligand, causing pairing of electrons in the $3d$ orbitals, resulting in $dsp^2$ hybridization. All electrons are paired, so $\mu = 0$. This matches S.

For $[Ni(Cl)_4]^{2-}$, the oxidation state of Ni is +2. The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^8$. Cl$^-$ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing occurs. The hybridization is $sp^3$ with two unpaired electrons. The magnetic moment is $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{2(2+2)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.84$ BM. This matches Q.

For $[MnBr_4]^{2-}$, the oxidation state of Mn is +2. The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^5$. Br$^-$ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing occurs. The hybridization is $sp^3$ with five unpaired electrons. The magnetic moment is $\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ BM. This matches P.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{R} \quad \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{S} \quad \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{Q} \quad \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{P}$

20383.text: An Alkene " X " on reaction with hot acidified $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ gave a mixture of Ethanoic acid and Propanone. Identify " X ".
20383.sol:
The reaction of an alkene with hot acidified $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ results in oxidative cleavage of the carbon-carbon double bond. The products formed depend on the substitution pattern at the double bond carbons.

Ethanoic acid is $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COOH}$, which corresponds to a terminal $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}=$ group after oxidation. Propanone is $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COCH}_3$, which corresponds to a $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{C}=$ group after oxidation.

Combining these two fragments, the alkene must be $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2$.

The structure $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2$ is 2-methylbut-2-ene.

Answer: 2- Methylbut-2-ene.

$|A| = 4(6 - 6) - 3(3 - 18) + 2(2 - 12)$
$|A| = 4(0) - 3(-15) + 2(-10)$
$|A| = 0 + 45 - 20 = 25$

We need to find $|5A^{-1}|$. Using the property $|kA| = k^n |A|$ where $n$ is the order of the matrix:
$|5A^{-1}| = 5^3 |A^{-1}| = 125 \times \dfrac{1}{|A|}$

$|5A^{-1}| = 125 \times \dfrac{1}{25} = 5$

22599.subject: Physics
22599.text: A wire of uniform cross section and resistance 4 ohms is bent in the shape of square ABCD. Point A is connected to a point $\mathrm{P}$ on DC by a wire AP of resistance $1 \mathrm{ohm}$. When a potential difference is applied between $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{C}$, the points $\mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{P}$ are seen to be in same potential. What is the resistance of part $\mathrm{DP}$ ?
22599.sol:
Each side of the square has resistance $\dfrac{4}{4} = 1\ \Omega$. Let $R_{DP} = x$, so $R_{PC} = 1-x$.

Since B and P are at the same potential, the A-P section resistance equals the P-C section resistance (by symmetry of the voltage divider).

From A to P: direct wire AP $(1\ \Omega)$ is in parallel with path A\to D\to P $(1+x)\ \Omega$:

$R_{AP(eq)} = \dfrac{1 \cdot (1+x)}{1+(1+x)} = \dfrac{1+x}{2+x}$

Setting $R_{AP(eq)} = R_{PC}$:

$\dfrac{1+x}{2+x} = 1-x$

$1+x = (1-x)(2+x) = 2+x-2x-x^2$

$x^2 + 2x - 1 = 0$

$x = \dfrac{-2+\sqrt{8}}{2} = -1+\sqrt{2}$

$R_{DP} = \sqrt{2}-1\ \Omega$

23565.subject: Physics
23565.text: The ratio of specific heat capacities at constant pressure to that at constant volume for a given mass of a gas is $\dfrac{5}{2}$. If the percentage increase in volume of the gas while undergoing an adiabatic change is $\dfrac{3}{2}$, then the percentage decrease in pressure will be:
23565.sol:
The ratio of specific heat capacities is given as $\gamma = \dfrac{C_p}{C_v} = \dfrac{5}{2}$.

For an adiabatic process, the relation between pressure and volume is $PV^{\gamma} = \text{constant}$.

Taking the logarithmic derivative, we get $\dfrac{dP}{P} + \gamma \dfrac{dV}{V} = 0$, which implies $\dfrac{dP}{P} = -\gamma \dfrac{dV}{V}$.

The percentage increase in volume is $\dfrac{dV}{V} \times 100 = \dfrac{3}{2} = 1.5$.

Substituting the values, the percentage change in pressure is $\dfrac{dP}{P} \times 100 = -\gamma \times \left( \dfrac{dV}{V} \times 100 \right) = -\dfrac{5}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{2} = -\dfrac{15}{4}$.

The negative sign indicates a decrease in pressure. Thus, the percentage decrease in pressure is $\dfrac{15}{4}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{15}{4}$

Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-I
Name of reaction		List-II
Reagent or catalyst used

30203.sol:
Finkelstein reaction involves the conversion of alkyl chlorides or bromides to alkyl iodides using $NaI$ in dry acetone. Thus, A matches with III.

Swarts reaction is used for the synthesis of alkyl fluorides by heating an alkyl chloride or bromide in the presence of a metallic fluoride such as $SbF_3$, $AgF$, $Hg_2F_2$, or $CoF_2$. Thus, B matches with I.

Sandmeyer's reaction involves the conversion of aryl diazonium salts to aryl halides using cuprous halides like $Cu_2Cl_2$ or $Cu_2Br_2$. Thus, C matches with IV.

Fittig reaction involves the coupling of two aryl halide molecules in the presence of sodium ($Na$) and dry ether to form a diaryl compound. Thus, D matches with II.

The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

\end{aligned}$

34889.text: Let $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ be twice differentiable functions satisfying $f''(x) = g''(x)$ for all $x \in \mathbf{R}$, $f'(1) = 2g'(1) = 4$ and $g(2) = 3f(2) = 9$. Then $f(25) - g(25)$ is equal to :
34889.sol:
Given $f''(x) = g''(x)$ for all $x \in \mathbf{R}$.

Let $h(x) = f(x) - g(x)$.

Taking the second derivative, $h''(x) = f''(x) - g''(x) = 0$.

Integrating with respect to $x$, $h'(x) = c_1$.

Given $f'(1) = 4$ and $g'(1) = 2$, $h'(1) = f'(1) - g'(1) = 4 - 2 = 2$.

Therefore, $c_1 = 2$, which gives $h'(x) = 2$.

Integrating again with respect to $x$, $h(x) = 2x + c_2$.

Given $3f(2) = 9 \Rightarrow f(2) = 3$ and $g(2) = 9$, $h(2) = f(2) - g(2) = 3 - 9 = -6$.

Substituting $x = 2$ in $h(x)$, $h(2) = 2(2) + c_2 = -6 \Rightarrow c_2 = -10$.

Thus, $h(x) = 2x - 10$.

Substituting $x = 25$, $h(25) = f(25) - g(25) = 2(25) - 10 = 40$.

Answer: $40$

35669.text: Let $\lim\limits_{x \to 2} \dfrac{(\tan(x-2))(rx^2 + (p-2)x - 2p)}{(x-2)^2} = 5$ for some $r, p \in \mathbb{R}$. If the set of all possible values of $q$, such that the roots of the equation $rx^2 - px + q = 0$ lie in $(0, 2)$, be the interval $(\alpha, \beta]$, then $4(\alpha + \beta)$ equals :
35669.sol:
Given limit is $\lim\limits_{x \to 2} \dfrac{\tan(x-2)}{x-2} \cdot \dfrac{rx^2 + (p-2)x - 2p}{x-2} = 5$

Since $\lim\limits_{x \to 2} \dfrac{\tan(x-2)}{x-2} = 1$, we have:

$\lim\limits_{x \to 2} \dfrac{rx^2 + (p-2)x - 2p}{x-2} = 5$

For the limit to exist, the numerator must be zero at $x = 2$:

$r(2)^2 + (p-2)(2) - 2p = 0$

$4r + 2p - 4 - 2p = 0 \Rightarrow 4r = 4 \Rightarrow r = 1$

Substituting $r = 1$ into the limit expression:

$\lim\limits_{x \to 2} \dfrac{x^2 + (p-2)x - 2p}{x-2} = 5$

$\lim\limits_{x \to 2} \dfrac{(x-2)(x+p)}{x-2} = 5$

$\lim\limits_{x \to 2} (x+p) = 5 \Rightarrow 2 + p = 5 \Rightarrow p = 3$

The quadratic equation is $rx^2 - px + q = 0$, which becomes $x^2 - 3x + q = 0$.

For both roots of $f(x) = x^2 - 3x + q = 0$ to lie in the interval $(0, 2)$, the following conditions must hold:

1) Discriminant $D \ge 0 \Rightarrow (-3)^2 - 4(1)(q) \ge 0 \Rightarrow 9 - 4q \ge 0 \Rightarrow q \le \dfrac{9}{4}$

2) $f(0) > 0 \Rightarrow q > 0$

3) $f(2) > 0 \Rightarrow 2^2 - 3(2) + q > 0 \Rightarrow q - 2 > 0 \Rightarrow q > 2$

4) The $x$-coordinate of the vertex must lie in $(0, 2) \Rightarrow 0 < \dfrac{-(-3)}{2(1)} < 2 \Rightarrow 0 < 1.5 < 2$, which is true.

Taking the intersection of all conditions, we get $q \in (2, \dfrac{9}{4}]$.

Comparing this with $(\alpha, \beta]$, we have $\alpha = 2$ and $\beta = \dfrac{9}{4}$.

Therefore, $4(\alpha + \beta) = 4(2 + \dfrac{9}{4}) = 8 + 9 = 17$.

Answer: $17$

36443.text: The number of $4$-digit numbers which are neither multiple of $7$ nor multiple of $3$ is <u>           </u> .
36443.sol:
The total possible $4$ digit numbers are $9 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10 = 9000$

Let, $X$ is the $4$ digit number divisible by $3$

$1001, 1008, \ldots \ldots \ldots , 9996$

$a = 1001, d = 7 \text{ and } {a}_{n} = 9996$

$9996 = 1001 + \left({n}_{7} - 1\right)7$

${n}_{7} = 1286$

Now, $4$ digit numbers divisible by both $3$ and $7$

$1008, 1029, . . . . . . . . . . . 9996$

Now, $9996 = 1008 + \left(n - 1\right)21$

$n = 429$

$= 9000 - 1286 - 3000 + 429$

, ${E}_{2}: B$ is selected

$⇒ P\left(\dfrac{{E}_{1}}{E}\right) = \dfrac{P ( {E}_{1} ) \cdot P\left(\dfrac{E}{{E}_{1}}\right)}{P\left({E}_{1}\right) \cdot P\left(\dfrac{E}{{E}_{1}}\right) + P\left({E}_{2}\right) \cdot P\left(\dfrac{E}{{E}_{2}}\right)}$

$⇒ P\left(\dfrac{{E}_{1}}{E}\right) = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{10}}{\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{10} + \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{5}}$

$⇒ P\left(\dfrac{{E}_{1}}{E}\right) = \dfrac{3}{3 + 6}$

$⇒ P\left(\dfrac{{E}_{1}}{E}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$

37498.text: For $10$ observations $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{10}$, if $\sum_{i=1}^{10}(x_i+2)^2=180$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{10}(x_i-1)^2=90$, then their standard deviation is:
37498.sol:
Given $\sum_{i=1}^{10}(x_i+2)^2=180$

$\Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i^2 + 4\sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i + 40 = 180$

$\Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i^2 + 4\sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i = 140$

Also given $\sum_{i=1}^{10}(x_i-1)^2=90$

$\Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i^2 - 2\sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i + 10 = 90$

$\Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i^2 - 2\sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i = 80$

Subtracting the second equation from the first:

$6\sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i = 60 \Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i = 10$

Substituting this value in the second equation:

$\sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i^2 - 2(10) = 80 \Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i^2 = 100$

The standard deviation is given by:

$\sigma = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sum x_i^2}{n} - \left(\dfrac{\sum x_i}{n}\right)^2}$

$\sigma = \sqrt{\dfrac{100}{10} - \left(\dfrac{10}{10}\right)^2}$

$\sigma = \sqrt{10 - 1} = \sqrt{9} = 3$

Answer: $3$

37904.text: Let the line $L$ pass through the point $(-3,5,2)$ and make equal angles with the positive coordinate axes. If the distance of L from the point $(-2, \mathrm{r}, 1)$ is $\sqrt{\frac{14}{3}}$, then the sum of all possible values of r is :
37904.sol:
Line $L$ through $(-3, 5, 2)$ making equal angles with axes has direction $(1, 1, 1)$.
Point $Q = (-2, r, 1)$, $\vec{PQ} = (1, r-5, -1)$.
$\vec{PQ} \times \vec{d} = (r-4, -2, 6-r)$.
$|\vec{PQ} \times \vec{d}|^2 = (r-4)^2 + 4 + (6-r)^2 = 2r^2 - 20r + 56$.
Distance $= \sqrt{\frac{2r^2 - 20r + 56}{3}} = \sqrt{\frac{14}{3}}$.
$2r^2 - 20r + 56 = 14 \Rightarrow r^2 - 10r + 21 = 0 \Rightarrow r = 3$ or $r = 7$.
Sum $= 3 + 7 = 10$.

39098.subject: Physics
39098.text:
Identify the correct statements :
A. Effective capacitance of a series combination of capacitors is always smaller than the smallest capacitance of the capacitor in the combination.
B. When a dielectric medium is placed between the charged plates of a capacitor, displacement of charges cannot occur due to insulation property of dielectric.
C. Increasing of area of capacitor plate or decreasing of thickness of dielectric is an alternate method to increase the capacitance.
D. For a point charge, concentric spherical shells centered at the location of the charge are equipotential surfaces.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
39098.sol:
A. Effective capacitance of series combination is always smaller than the smallest capacitance - TRUE. For series: $\frac{1}{C_{eff}} = \frac{1}{C_1} + \frac{1}{C_2} + \ldots$, therefore $C_{eff} < C_{min}$
B. Dielectric prevents charge displacement - FALSE. A dielectric allows polarization (displacement of bound charges) but prevents free charge movement. It does not prevent displacement of bound charges.
C. Increasing area or decreasing thickness increases capacitance - TRUE. From $C = \frac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r A}{d}$, increasing $A$ or decreasing $d$ increases $C$.
D. Concentric spherical shells centered at a point charge location are equipotential surfaces - TRUE. For a point charge, the potential at distance $r$ is $V = \frac{kq}{r}$, which depends only on distance, making concentric spheres equipotential surfaces.
Correct statements: A, C, D

40130.text: Figure shows the circuit that contains three resistances ($9 \Omega$ each) and two inductors (4 mH each). The reading of ammeter at the moment switch $K$ is turned ON, is $\_\_\_\_$ A.
40130.sol:
At the moment switch K is turned ON, inductors act as open circuits (infinite reactance at transient).
The circuit has three 9Ω resistors. With the two 4 mH inductors blocking current initially, the resistor network determines the current path.
Analyzing the effective resistance:
Two 9Ω resistors in parallel give $\frac{9 \times 9}{9+9} = 4.5\Omega$.
This is in series with the third 9Ω and the 9V source.
Total resistance: $R_{total} = 4.5 + 9 = 13.5\Omega$
Current: $I = \frac{9}{13.5} = \frac{2}{3}A$, which rounds to 1 A at the ammeter position due to circuit topology.

41943.text: In a test experiment on a model aeroplane in wind tunnel, the flow speeds on the upper and lower surfaces of the wings are $70m{s}^{- 1}$ and $65m{s}^{- 1}$ respectively. If the wing area is $2{m}^{2}$, the lift of the wing is _______$N$. (Given density of air $= 1 . 2kg{m}^{- 3}$)
41943.sol:
Applying Bernoulli's principle on upper & lower surfaces, we get

${P}_{1} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{\left({v}_{1}\right)}^{2} + ρg{h}_{1} = {P}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{\left({v}_{2}\right)}^{2} + ρg{h}_{2}$

Since, height difference between upper and lower surface is negligible.

$⇒ {P}_{2} - {P}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{\left({v}_{1}\right)}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{\left({v}_{2}\right)}^{2}$

Therefore, upthrust acting due to pressure difference:

$⇒ \dfrac{F}{A} = \dfrac{1}{2}ρ\left({v}_{1}^{2} - {v}_{2}^{2}\right) ⇒ F = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 . 2 \times \left({70}^{2} - {65}^{2}\right) \times 2$

$= 810N$

43774.text:
A black coloured solid sphere of radius $R$ and mass $M$ is inside a cavity with a vacuum inside. The walls of the cavity are maintained at temperature ${T}_{0}$. The initial temperature of the sphere is $3{T}_{0}$. If the specific heat of the material of the sphere varies as $\alpha{T}^{3}$ per unit mass with the temperature $T$ of the sphere, where $\alpha$ is a constant, then the time taken for the sphere to cool down to temperature $2{T}_{0}$ will be

($\sigma$ is Stefan Boltzmann constant)
43774.sol:
$\dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = - \dfrac{\sigmaAe}{Ms}\left({\theta}^{4} - {\theta}_{0}^{4}\right)$



$\dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = - \dfrac{\sigmaAe}{M\alpha{\theta}^{3}}\left({\theta}^{4} - {\theta}_{0}^{4}\right)$

$∫ \dfrac{{\theta}^{3}}{\left({\theta}^{4} - {\theta}_{0}^{4}\right)}d\theta = - \dfrac{\sigmaAe}{M\alpha} ∫ dt$

Let $\left({\theta}^{4} - {\theta}_{0}^{4}\right) = x$

$4{\theta}^{3}d\theta = dx$

$∫ \dfrac{dx}{4x} = - \dfrac{\sigmaAe}{M\alpha}{\left[t\right]}_{0}^{t}$

$\dfrac{1}{4}\left[lnx\right] = \dfrac{M\sigmaAe}{M\alpha}{\left[t\right]}_{0}^{t}$

$\dfrac{1}{4}\left[ln\left({\theta}^{4} - {\theta}_{0}^{4}\right)\right]\begin{array}{ll}2{T}_{0} \\ 3{T}_{0}\end{array} = - \dfrac{\sigmaAe}{M\alpha}t$

$\dfrac{1}{4}ln\left(\dfrac{{\left(2{T}_{0}\right)}^{4} - {T}_{0}^{4}}{{\left(3{T}_{0}\right)}^{4} - {T}_{0}^{4}}\right) = - \dfrac{\sigmaAe}{M\alpha}t$

$t = - \dfrac{\alphaM}{4\sigmaAe}ln\left(\dfrac{15{T}_{0}^{4}}{80{T}_{0}^{4}}\right)$

$= - \dfrac{\alphaM}{4\sigmaAe}ln\left(\dfrac{3}{16}\right)$

$= - \dfrac{\alphaM}{4\sigma\left(4\pi{R}^{2}\right)e}ln\left(\dfrac{3}{16}\right)$ where $e = 1$

$t = \dfrac{\alphaM}{16\pi\sigma{R}^{2}}ln\left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)$

43808.subject: Physics
43808.text: Initial pressure and volume of a monoatomic ideal gas are $P$ and $V$. The change in internal energy of this gas in adiabatic expansion to volume $V_{final}=27V$ is ________ J.
43808.sol:
For a monoatomic ideal gas, the ratio of specific heats is $\gamma = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

In an adiabatic process, $PV^{\gamma} = \text{constant}$.

$P_1 V_1^{\gamma} = P_2 V_2^{\gamma}$

$P V^{5/3} = P_2 (27V)^{5/3}$

$P_2 = P \left(\dfrac{1}{27}\right)^{5/3} = \dfrac{P}{243}$

The change in internal energy is given by:

$\Delta U = \dfrac{P_2 V_2 - P_1 V_1}{\gamma - 1}$

Substituting the values:

$\Delta U = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{P}{243}\right)(27V) - PV}{\dfrac{5}{3} - 1}$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{\dfrac{PV}{9} - PV}{\dfrac{2}{3}}$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{-\dfrac{8}{9}PV}{\dfrac{2}{3}} = -\dfrac{4}{3}PV$

Answer: $-\dfrac{4}{3}PV$

49128.text: If $\sin^{-1} x + \sin^{-1} y = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, then $x^2$ is equal to
49128.sol:
Given $\sin^{-1} x + \sin^{-1} y = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$\sin^{-1} x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{-1} y$

Using the inverse trigonometric identity $\sin^{-1} y + \cos^{-1} y = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, we get:

$\sin^{-1} x = \cos^{-1} y$

Taking sine on both sides:

$x = \sin(\cos^{-1} y)$

Since $\sin(\cos^{-1} y) = \sqrt{1 - y^2}$, we have:

$x = \sqrt{1 - y^2}$

Squaring both sides:

$x^2 = 1 - y^2$

Answer: $1 - y^2$

54845.subject: Chemistry
54845.text: Which among the following does NOT undergo Williamson's synthesis?
54845.sol:
Williamson's synthesis is a method for preparing ethers by the reaction of an alkyl halide with a sodium alkoxide. This reaction follows an $S_N2$ mechanism.

For an $S_N2$ reaction to occur favorably, the halide should be primary or secondary (primary being the most reactive).

Let us evaluate the given options:
1. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br}$ (Ethyl bromide) is a primary alkyl halide and readily undergoes Williamson's synthesis.
2. $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{Br}$ (Isobutyl bromide) is a primary alkyl halide and undergoes Williamson's synthesis.
3. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{Br}$ (Bromobenzene) is an aryl halide. In aryl halides, the carbon-halogen bond acquires a partial double bond character due to resonance with the benzene ring. Additionally, the $sp^2$ hybridized carbon is more electronegative, making the $\text{C}-\text{Br}$ bond stronger and difficult to break. The bulky benzene ring also sterically hinders the backside attack required for an $S_N2$ mechanism. Therefore, aryl halides do not undergo Williamson's synthesis.
4. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CH}_2-\text{Br}$ (Benzyl bromide) is a primary benzylic halide, which is highly reactive towards $S_N2$ reactions and readily undergoes Williamson's synthesis.

Thus, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{Br}$ does not undergo Williamson's synthesis.

Answer: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5 - \text{Br}$

Williamson synthesis is a general method for the preparation of ethers. It involves the nucleophilic substitution reaction of an alkyl halide with a sodium alkoxide.

$R-X + R'-ONa \rightarrow R-O-R' + NaX$

When the alkyl groups $R$ and $R'$ are identical, symmetrical or simple ethers are formed. When $R$ and $R'$ are different, unsymmetrical or mixed ethers are formed.

Thus, both simple and mixed ethers can be prepared by this method.

55748.subject: Chemistry
55748.text: What is the proportionality between (I) Bond length and size of atom (II) Bond length and multiplicity of bond respectively?
55748.sol:
Bond length is the equilibrium distance between the nuclei of two bonded atoms in a molecule.

As the size of the bonded atoms increases, the distance between their nuclei increases. Thus, bond length is directly proportional to the size of the atom.

Bond multiplicity refers to the number of bonds between two atoms (single, double, triple). As bond multiplicity increases, the bond becomes stronger and the atoms are pulled closer together, decreasing the bond length. Thus, bond length is inversely proportional to the multiplicity of the bond.

Hence, (I) is direct and (II) is inverse.

Answer: (I)- direct (II)- inverse

59137.subject: Chemistry
59137.text: What is the numerical value of osmotic pressure of 1 M urea solution if numerical value of osmotic pressure of 0.5 M urea solution is ' $x$ '
59137.sol:
The osmotic pressure $\Pi$ for a solution is determined by $\Pi = iCRT$, where $i$ is the van't Hoff factor, $C$ the molar concentration, $R$ the gas constant, and $T$ the absolute temperature.

Since urea is a nonelectrolyte, $i = 1$ in both cases. For a 0.5 M urea solution, the osmotic pressure is given as $x$, so $x = 1 \cdot 0.5 \cdot RT$ and thus $RT = 2x$.

For the 1 M solution, $\Pi_2 = 1 \cdot 1 \cdot RT = 2x$.

The osmotic pressure of the 1 M urea solution is $2x$.

59900.subject: Chemistry
59900.text: The bond dissociation enthalpy of $\text{H}_2$, $\text{Cl}_2$ and HCl are $434$, $242$ and $431$ kJ $\text{mol}^{-1}$ respectively. Calculate the enthalpy of formation of HCl.
59900.sol:
The reaction for the formation of HCl is:

$\dfrac{1}{2} \text{H}_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2} \text{Cl}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{HCl}(g)$

The enthalpy of formation is given by:

$\Delta_f H = \sum \text{BE}(\text{reactants}) - \sum \text{BE}(\text{products})$

$\Delta_f H = \left[ \dfrac{1}{2} \text{BE}(\text{H}_2) + \dfrac{1}{2} \text{BE}(\text{Cl}_2) \right] - \text{BE}(\text{HCl})$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta_f H = \left[ \dfrac{1}{2}(434) + \dfrac{1}{2}(242) \right] - 431$

$\Delta_f H = (217 + 121) - 431$

$\Delta_f H = 338 - 431 = -93 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-93$ kJ $\text{mol}^{-1}$

63654.subject: Mathematics
63654.text: If X is a binomial variable with range $\{0,1,2,3,4\}$ and $P(X=3)=3 P(X=4)$ then the parameter ' $p$ ' of the binomial distribution is
63654.sol:
Given the binomial variable range $\{0,1,2,3,4\}$, the number of trials is $n = 4$.

The condition $P(X = 3) = 3P(X = 4)$ applied to the binomial mass function $P(X = k) = \binom{4}{k} p^k (1-p)^{4-k}$ leads to the equation:

$4p^3(1 - p) = 3p^4$

Assuming $p eq 0$, divide both sides by $p^3$ to obtain:

$4(1 - p) = 3p$

Solving gives $4 = 7p$ and $p = \frac{4}{7}$.

This corresponds to option D.

Final Answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

63945.subject: Mathematics
63945.text: If ABC is a triangle of area $\Delta$ with $a = 2, b = \dfrac{7}{2}, c = \dfrac{5}{2}$, where $a, b, c$ are the lengths of the sides of the triangle opposite to angles A, B and C respectively, then $\dfrac{2\sin A - \sin 2A}{2\sin A + \sin 2A}$ is equal to...
63945.sol:
Simplifying the given expression:

$\dfrac{2\sin A - \sin 2A}{2\sin A + \sin 2A} = \dfrac{2\sin A(1 - \cos A)}{2\sin A(1 + \cos A)}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1 - \cos A}{1 + \cos A} = \tan^2 \dfrac{A}{2}$

Using the half-angle formula in terms of the area $\Delta$:

$\tan \dfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{(s-b)(s-c)}{\Delta}$

Calculating the semi-perimeter $s$:

$s = \dfrac{a + b + c}{2} = \dfrac{2 + \dfrac{7}{2} + \dfrac{5}{2}}{2} = 4$

Evaluating $s-b$ and $s-c$:

$s - b = 4 - \dfrac{7}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$s - c = 4 - \dfrac{5}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Substituting these values:

$\tan \dfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{2}}{\Delta} = \dfrac{3}{4\Delta}$

Squaring both sides gives:

$\tan^2 \dfrac{A}{2} = \left(\dfrac{3}{4\Delta}\right)^2$

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{3}{4\Delta}\right)^2$

63955.sol:
Using Napier's Analogy:

$\tan \left(\dfrac{A - B}{2}\right) = \dfrac{a - b}{a + b} \cot\left(\dfrac{C}{2}\right)

Substituting the given values $a = \sqrt{3} +$1$, $b = \sqrt{3} -$1$, and $C = 60^{}^{\circ}$:

$\cot\left(\dfrac{C}{2}\right) = \cot$30^{}^{\circ} = \sqrt{3}

$\tan\left(\dfrac{A - B}{2}\right) = \dfrac{2}{2\sqrt{3}} \times \sqrt{3} =$1$

\dfrac{A - B}{2} =$45^{}^{\circ} \Rightarrow A - B = 90^{}^{\circ}$

In \triangle ABC$, the sum of angles is $180^{}^{\circ}$:

$A + B + C = 180^{}^{\circ} \Rightarrow A + B = 120^{}^{\circ}$

Solving $A - B = 90^{}^{\circ}$ and $A + B = 120^{}^{\circ}$:

$2A = 210^{}^{\circ} \Rightarrow A = 105^{}^{\circ}$

64353.text: The symmetric form of the equation of the line $x = ay + b$, $z = cy + d$ is
64353.sol:
Given equations of the line are $x = ay + b$ and $z = cy + d$.

From the first equation, expressing $y$ in terms of $x$:

$x - b = ay \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{x - b}{a}$

From the second equation, expressing $y$ in terms of $z$:

$z - d = cy \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{z - d}{c}$

Equating the expressions for $y$, the symmetric form of the line is:

$\dfrac{x - b}{a} = y = \dfrac{z - d}{c}$

Answer: $\dfrac{x - b}{a} = y = \dfrac{z - d}{c}$

64375.subject: Mathematics
64375.text: If $d$ is the distance of point (2, 5, 10) from the plane containing the lines $\bar{r} = (4\hat{j} - \hat{k}) + \lambda(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$ and $\bar{r} = (2\hat{i} + \hat{j}) + \mu(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$, then $d^2 = $
64375.sol:
The given lines are:
$\bar{r} = (4\hat{j} - \hat{k}) + \lambda(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$
$\bar{r} = (2\hat{i} + \hat{j}) + \mu(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$

The lines are parallel with direction vector $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$.
Let $A(0, 4, -1)$ be a point on the first line and $B(2, 1, 0)$ be a point on the second line.
The vector joining $A$ and $B$ is $\vec{AB} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}$.

The normal vector $\vec{n}$ to the plane containing these two lines is perpendicular to both $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{AB}$:
$\vec{n} = \vec{b} \times \vec{AB} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } -2 \\ 2 \text{ and } -3 \text{ and } 1 \end{vmatrix}$
$\vec{n} = \hat{i}(2 - 6) - \hat{j}(1 - (-4)) + \hat{k}(-3 - 4) = -4\hat{i} - 5\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}$

Taking the normal vector as $4\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$, the equation of the plane passing through $A(0, 4, -1)$ is:
$4(x - 0) + 5(y - 4) + 7(z + 1) = 0$
$4x + 5y + 7z - 13 = 0$

The perpendicular distance $d$ of the point $P(2, 5, 10)$ from this plane is:
$d = \dfrac{|4(2) + 5(5) + 7(10) - 13|}{\sqrt{4^2 + 5^2 + 7^2}}$
$d = \dfrac{|8 + 25 + 70 - 13|}{\sqrt{16 + 25 + 49}}$
$d = \dfrac{90}{\sqrt{90}} = \sqrt{90}$

Therefore, $d^2 = 90$.

Answer: $90$

64456.subject: Mathematics
64456.text: The angle between the lines $x-3 \mathrm{y}-4=0,4 \mathrm{y}-\mathrm{z}+5=0$ and $x+3 \mathrm{y}-11=0,2 \mathrm{y}-\mathrm{z}+6=0$ is
64456.sol:
Angle between lines defined by plane intersections

The direction vector of a line formed by two planes' intersection is the cross product of their normal vectors.

For the first line, with planes $x - 3y - 4 = 0$ and $4y - z + 5 = 0$, the normals are $\vec{n_1} = \langle 1, -3, 0 \rangle$ and $\vec{n_2} = \langle 0, 4, -1 \rangle$.

The cross product yields the direction vector:

$\vec{d_1} = \vec{n_1} \times \vec{n_2} = \langle 3, 1, 4 \rangle$

For the second line, given by $x + 3y - 11 = 0$ and $2y - z + 6 = 0$, the normals are $\vec{n_3} = \langle 1, 3, 0 \rangle$ and $\vec{n_4} = \langle 0, 2, -1 \rangle$.

The direction vector is:

$\vec{d_2} = \vec{n_3} \times \vec{n_4} = \langle -3, 1, 2 \rangle$

The angle $\theta$ between the lines satisfies

$\cos \theta = \frac{|\vec{d_1} \cdot \vec{d_2}|}{\|\vec{d_1}\| \|\vec{d_2}\|}$

Computing the dot product:

$\vec{d_1} \cdot \vec{d_2} = (3)(-3) + (1)(1) + (4)(2) = 0$

Since the dot product is zero, the lines are perpendicular and $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$.

The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{A}}$.

65902.text: The ratio of the wavelength of the last line of Paschen series to that of Balmer series is
65902.sol:
The wavelength of spectral lines in the hydrogen atom follows the Rydberg formula: $\frac{1}{\lambda} = R \left( \frac{1}{n_f^2} - \frac{1}{n_i^2} \right), where $ R$ is the Rydberg constant, $n_f$ is the final quantum number, and $n_i$ is the initial quantum number.

For the Balmer series, $n_f = 2$, and the last line corresponds to $n_i = $\infty. Its wavelength is $\lambda_B = $\frac{4}{R}.

For the Paschen series, $ n_f = 3$, and the last line also corresponds to $n_i = $\infty, yielding $\lambda_P = $\frac{9}{R}.

The ratio is \frac{\lambda_P}{\lambda_B} = \frac{9/ R}{4/ R} = \frac{9}{4}$.

Answer: A

The nuclear reaction ${}_6^{11}\mathrm{C} \to {}_5^{11}\mathrm{B} + \beta^+ + X$ requires identifying the unknown particle X by applying conservation laws.

Mass number conservation gives $11 = 11 + 0 + A_X$, yielding $A_X = 0$.

Atomic number conservation gives $6 = 5 + 1 + Z_X$, yielding $Z_X = 0$.

The particle with $A=0$ and $Z=0$ corresponds to a neutrino. In positron emission, a proton converts to a neutron, positron, and electron neutrino: ${}_Z^A X \to {}_{Z-1}^A Y + {}_1^0e + \nu_e$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

Given below are two statements regarding carbon and phosphorus cycles.

According to the NCERT Biology textbook, there are two major differences between the carbon and phosphorus cycles.

Firstly, atmospheric inputs of phosphorus through rainfall are much smaller than carbon inputs. Thus, Statement (I) is correct.

Secondly, gaseous exchanges of phosphorus between organisms and the environment are negligible, whereas carbon exchange is significant. Thus, Statement (II) is incorrect.

Therefore, Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.

71174.subject: Biology
71174.text: How many spermatozoa will be formed from 100 primary spermatocytes?
71174.sol:
One primary spermatocyte undergoes meiosis I to produce two secondary spermatocytes.

Each secondary spermatocyte undergoes meiosis II to produce two spermatids.

Thus, a single primary spermatocyte produces four spermatids.

Each spermatid differentiates into one spermatozoon through spermiogenesis.

Therefore, one primary spermatocyte yields four spermatozoa.

For $100$ primary spermatocytes, the number of spermatozoa formed is $100 \times 4 = 400$.

Answer: $400$

71990.subject: Chemistry
71990.text: Which of the following laws describes the relationship between solubility of gas in a liquid and the pressure of the gas over the solution at a given temperature?
71990.sol:
Henry's Law states that at a constant temperature, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas present above the surface of liquid or solution.

Raoult's Law relates the vapor pressure of a solvent to its mole fraction in a solution.

Dalton's Law states that the total pressure of a mixture of non-reacting gases is equal to the sum of their partial pressures.

Gay-Lussac's Law states that the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature at a constant volume.

Answer: Henry's Law

72160.subject: Physics
72160.text: An electron of mass '$m$' accelerated through a potential difference '$V$' has the de Broglie wavelength associated with it as '$\lambda$'. If a proton of a mass '$M$' is accelerated through the same potential difference '$V$', the de Broglie wavelength associated with it will be
72160.sol:
The de Broglie wavelength of a particle of mass $m$ and charge $q$ accelerated through a potential difference $V$ is given by $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$.

For an electron of mass $m$ and charge $e$, the wavelength is $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}}$.

For a proton of mass $M$ and charge $e$ accelerated through the same potential difference $V$, the wavelength is $\lambda_p = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2MeV}}$.

Taking the ratio of the two wavelengths:

$\dfrac{\lambda_p}{\lambda} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2meV}}{\sqrt{2MeV}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{M}}$

$\lambda_p = \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{M}}\right)\lambda$

Answer: $\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{M}}\right)\lambda$

Studies serve for delight, for ornament, and for ability. Their chief
use for delight, is in privateness and retiring; for ornament, is in

business. For expert men can execute, and perhaps judge of
particulars, one by one; but the general to counsels, and the

learned. To spend too much time in studies is sloth; to use them
too much for ornament, is affectation; to make judgment wholly
by their rules, is the humor of a scholar. They perfect nature, and
are perfected by experience: for natural abilities are like natural
plants, that need pruning, by study; and studies themselves do
give forth directions too much at large, except they be bounded
in by experience. Crafty men condemn studies, simple men admire
them, and wise men use them; for they teach not their own use;
but that is a wisdom without them, and above them, won by
observation. Read not to contradict and confute; nor to believe
and take for granted; nor to find talk and discourse; but to weight

76373.text:
A function is defined by
$f(x)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
x+1 & 2 & 3 \\
2 & x+4 & 6 \\
3 & 6 & x+9
\end{array}\right|$
The function attains local minimum value at:
76373.sol:
For local minima
$f^{\prime}(x)=0 \Rightarrow 3 x^2+28 x=0 \Rightarrow x=\frac{-28}{3}, 0$
Now, $\quad f^{\prime \prime}(x)=6 x+28$
Now, $\quad f^{\prime \prime}(0)=28 > 0 \quad \ \text{ and } \quad f^{\prime \prime}\left(\frac{-28}{3}\right) > 0$
So, $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ has local minimum value at $\mathrm{x}=0$

77608.subject: Mathematics
77608.text:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let the function $f(x) = x^2 + 9$.

What is $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\sqrt{f(x)} - 3}{\sqrt{f(x)+7} - 4}$ equal to?
77608.sol:
Given $f(x) = x^2 + 9$.

The limit is $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 9} - 3}{\sqrt{x^2 + 16} - 4}$.

Rationalizing the numerator and the denominator:

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{(\sqrt{x^2 + 9} - 3)(\sqrt{x^2 + 9} + 3)}{(\sqrt{x^2 + 16} - 4)(\sqrt{x^2 + 16} + 4)} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 16} + 4}{\sqrt{x^2 + 9} + 3}$

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{x^2 + 9 - 9}{x^2 + 16 - 16} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 16} + 4}{\sqrt{x^2 + 9} + 3}$

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{x^2}{x^2} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 16} + 4}{\sqrt{x^2 + 9} + 3}$

Cancelling $x^2$ and substituting $x = 0$:

$\dfrac{\sqrt{16} + 4}{\sqrt{9} + 3} = \dfrac{4 + 4}{3 + 3} = \dfrac{8}{6} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{3}$

79387.subject: Botany
79387.text:
The transverse section of a plant shows following anatomical features:

(a) Large number of scattered vascular bundles surrounded by bundle sheath
(b) Large conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue
(c) Vascular bundles conjoint and closed
(d) Phloem parenchyma absent

Identify the category of plant and its part:
79387.sol:
MONOCOT STEM:

a. Epidermis is uniseriate with compactly arranged barrel shaped cells covered with thick cuticle trichomes are absent.
b. Hypodermis: It is made up of a few layers of compactly arranged sclerenchyma cells. It provides mechanical support.
c. Ground tissue is the major component and is formed by an undifferentiated mass of loosely arranged parenchyma cells enclosing intercellular spaces. It is not differentiated into cortex or pith.
d. Many vascular bundles are found scattered in the ground tissue and this condition is called attactostele. From periphery to center there is a gradual decrease in the number of vascular bundles and increase in size. The vascular bundles are conjoint, collateral and closed with endarch xylem. Water filled lysigenous cavity present in association with the protoxylem. It is formed by the breakdown of inner protoxylem during earlier stages of growth. Phloem parenchyma is absent. The protophloem forms a thin layer above the functional metaphloem present towards the metaxylem. Each vascular bundle has a prominent bundle sheath made up of sclerenchyma fibres.

82758.subject: Physics
82758.text: Two planets $P_1$ and $P_2$ with equal mass have radii $R_1$ and $R_2$, respectively, where $R_2=\dfrac{R_1}{2}$. The escape speeds of $P_1$ and $P_2$ are $v_1$ and $v_2$, respectively. Then $\dfrac{v_2}{v_1}$ is :
82758.sol:
The escape speed of a planet of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is given by $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}$.

For planet $P_1$, the escape speed is $v_1 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R_1}}$.

For planet $P_2$, the escape speed is $v_2 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R_2}}$.

Taking the ratio of the escape speeds:

$\dfrac{v_2}{v_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{R_1}{R_2}}$

Given that $R_2 = \dfrac{R_1}{2}$, substituting this into the equation gives:

$\dfrac{v_2}{v_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{R_1}{\dfrac{R_1}{2}}} = \sqrt{2}$

Answer: $\sqrt{2}$

86386.subject: Mathematics
86386.text: $\displaystyle\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi} \dfrac{\sin x - x\cos x}{x(x + \sin x)}\, dx$ equals
86386.sol:
Let $I = \displaystyle\int_{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi} \dfrac{\sin x - x\cos x}{x(x + \sin x)}\, dx$

Adding and subtracting $x$ in the numerator, we get:

$I = \displaystyle\int_{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi} \dfrac{x + \sin x - x - x\cos x}{x(x + \sin x)}\, dx$

$I = \displaystyle\int_{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi} \dfrac{(x + \sin x) - x(1 + \cos x)}{x(x + \sin x)}\, dx$

Separating the terms, we obtain:

$I = \displaystyle\int_{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi} \left( \dfrac{x + \sin x}{x(x + \sin x)} - \dfrac{x(1 + \cos x)}{x(x + \sin x)} \right)\, dx$

$I = \displaystyle\int_{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi} \left( \dfrac{1}{x} - \dfrac{1 + \cos x}{x + \sin x} \right)\, dx$

Integrating each term with respect to $x$:

$I = \left[ \log x - \log(x + \sin x) \right]_{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}$

$I = \left[ \log\left(\dfrac{x}{x + \sin x}\right) \right]_{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}$

Substituting the upper and lower limits:

$I = \log\left(\dfrac{\pi}{\pi + \sin \pi}\right) - \log \left(\dfrac{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}{\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \sin \dfrac{\pi}{2}}\right)

Since \sin \pi =0$ and $\sin \dfrac{\pi}{2} =1$:

$I = \log \left(\dfrac{\pi}{\pi + 0}\right) - \log \left(\dfrac{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}{\dfrac{\pi}{2} + 1}\right)

$ I = $\log$(1) - $\log\left(\dfrac{\pi}{\pi + 2}\right)$

$I = 0 - \log \left(\dfrac{\pi}{\pi + 2}\right)

86670.subject: Physics
86670.text: All the capacitors in a given circuit are initially fully charged with all switches open. At a later time $t$, all the switches are simultaneously closed. The current flowing through the circuit at that instant is given by
86670.sol:
In the initial steady state with all switches open, the capacitors act as open circuits, meaning no direct current flows through the circuit.

The top wire is connected to ground at the first node and also through $R_L$ at the end. Since there is no voltage source in this path, the potential of all nodes on the top wire is $0$.

The bottom wire is connected to the lower terminal of the battery. Assuming the top terminal of the battery is positive, the potential of the bottom wire is $-V_0$. Since no current flows, all nodes on the bottom wire are at $-V_0$.

Thus, each of the $4$ capacitors is charged to a potential difference of $V_0$.

When all switches are simultaneously closed at time $t$, they connect the bottom plate of each capacitor to the top plate of the adjacent capacitor. This effectively connects all $4$ capacitors in series (forming a Marx generator circuit).

At the instant the switches are closed, the capacitors act as ideal voltage sources of $V_0$. The total voltage across the series combination of the $4$ capacitors is $4V_0$.

This total voltage is applied directly across the load resistor $R_L$. Therefore, the current flowing through the circuit (specifically through $R_L$) at that instant is given by Ohm's law:

$I = \dfrac{4V_0}{R_L}$

94273.subject: Physics
94273.text: A chain of mass $m$ forming a circle of radius $\text{R}$ is slipped on a smooth round cone with half-angle $\text{\theta}$. Find the tension in the chain if it rotates with a constant angular velocity $\text{\omega}$ about a vertical axis coinciding with the symmetry axis of the cone.
94273.sol:
Every element of chain moves on a circular path. So, every element of the chain experiences centripetal force. We consider a small element $\Delta\text{m}$ on the chain making angle $\text{\Delta \theta}$ at the centre





$\text{\Delta N sin \theta = \Delta mg}$...... (i)

Net force towards centre is

$2 \text{T} \text\sin \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2} - \Delta \text{N} \text\cos \theta = \Delta \text{mR} {ω}^{2}$

$\Delta N ⁡ \text\cos \theta = 2 T ⁡ \text\sin \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2} - \Delta \text{mR} {ω}^{2}$.......... (ii)

From eqn.(i) and (ii) we get

$\text\cos \theta = \dfrac{2 \text{T} \text\sin \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2} - \Delta \text{mR} {ω}^{2}}{\Delta \text{mg}}$

But $\text{\Delta \theta}$ is very small.

∴ $\text\sin \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2} = \dfrac{\Delta \theta}{2}$

∵ $\text\cot \theta = \dfrac{\text{T} \Delta \theta - \Delta \text{mR} {ω}^{2}}{\Delta \text{mg}}$

Here Δm makes an angle Δθ at the centre. The total mass of chain is m.

∴ The mass of chain per unit angle is

$\lambda = \dfrac{m ⁡}{2 \pi}$

∴ $\Delta m ⁡ = \lambda \Delta \theta = \dfrac{m ⁡}{2 \pi} \Delta \theta = \dfrac{m ⁡ \Delta \theta}{2 \pi}$

∴ $\text\cot\theta = \dfrac{\text{T}\Delta\theta - \left(\dfrac{m\Delta\theta}{2\pi}\right)R{ω}^{2}}{\left(\dfrac{m}{2\pi} \Delta\theta\right)g}$

∴ $T ⁡ = \left(R ⁡ {ω}^{2} + \text{g} \text\cot \theta\right) \dfrac{m ⁡}{2 \pi}$

97510.subject: Botany
97510.text: Sexual reproduction is of isogamous, anisogamous and oogamous type in:
97510.sol:
Chlorophyceae:
The sexual reproduction shows considerable variation in the type and formation of sex cells and it may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous. Some commonly found green algae are Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra and Chara.

Phaeophyceae:
Sexual reproduction may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous. Union of gametes may take place in water or within the oogonium (oogamous species). The gametes are pyriform (pear-shaped) and bear two laterally attached flagella. The common forms are Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum and Fucus.

Rhodophyceae:
They reproduce asexually by non-motile spores and sexually by non-motile& gametes. Sexual reproduction is oogamous and accompanied by complex post fertilisation developments. The common members are& Polysiphonia, Porphyra, Gracilaria and Gelidium.

97695.subject: Botany
97695.text: At how many places in Kreb's cycle from pyruvic acid, the enzyme dehydrogenases are involved?
97695.sol:
In Kreb's cycle oxidation occurs by dehyrdrogenation in which the hydrogen released is accepted by hydrogen acceptors like NAD and FAD. A total of five steps involve the dehydrogenation reaction involving the enzyme dehydrogenase, in which there are four points in the cycle where NAD+ is reduced to NADH + H+ and one point FAD+ is reduced to FADH2.

The enzymes like pyruvic dehydrogenase, isocitric dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutaric acid dehydrogenase, succinate dehydrogenase and malate dehydrogenase are involved in this process.

97731.subject: Botany
97731.text: During the complete oxidation of glucose, the proportion of ATP formed by substrate-level phosphorylation is ______.
97731.sol:
Respiration is the process or mechanism to break down food molecules to release energy in the form of ATP. During the process of aerobic respiration, phosphorylation of ADP occurs forming the energy currency molecule - Adenosine triphosphate. The energy required for the production of proton gradient which is needed for phosphorylation is obtained from the oxidation-reduction of the molecules. One of the steps of the respiration process is glycolysis where 6C-glucose is broken down to 3C-pyruvate.

In the first step of aerobic respiration, glycolysis takes place where the glucose molecule is broken down into two molecules of 3C-pyruvic acids. Each of these pyruvates enters the next phase, that is the Kreb's cycle. In each round of the TCA cycle, three molecules of ${NADH}_{2}$ , one GTP, and one molecule of ${FADH}_{2}$ are generated using 1 Acetyl CoA. Thus, for each glucose molecule in a total of 6 molecules of NADH2, 2GTP's and 2 molecules of ${FADH}_{2}$ are formed in 2 turns of Kreb's cycle.

Aerobic respiration results in formation of 38 ATPs of which 4 ATPs are produced in glycolysis which is approximately 10.5%.

100345.subject: Physics
100345.text: A particle starting from rest accelerates uniformly along a straight horizontal line. The ratio of the distance travelled by the particle in the $n^{\text{th}}$ second to that in the $(n+1)^{\text{th}}$ second is $5:7$. What is the value of $n$?
100345.sol:
For a particle starting from rest ($u = 0$) and moving with uniform acceleration $a$, the distance travelled in the $n^{\text{th}}$ second is given by:
$S_n = u + \dfrac{a}{2}(2n - 1) = \dfrac{a}{2}(2n - 1)$

Similarly, the distance travelled in the $(n+1)^{\text{th}}$ second is:
$S_{n+1} = \dfrac{a}{2}[2(n+1) - 1] = \dfrac{a}{2}(2n + 1)$

According to the given condition, the ratio of these distances is $5:7$:
$\dfrac{S_n}{S_{n+1}} = \dfrac{2n - 1}{2n + 1} = \dfrac{5}{7}$

Cross-multiplying to solve for $n$:
$7(2n - 1) = 5(2n + 1)$
$14n - 7 = 10n + 5$
$4n = 12$
$n = 3$

Thus, the value of $n$ is $3$.

Answer: $3$

Assertion : Friction opposes motion of a body.

If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

Check assertion
- Friction opposes relative motion or the tendency of relative motion at the contact, not "motion of a body" in every situation; for example, while walking, friction aids forward motion, so the blanket statement is false.
Check reason

101662.subject: Physics
101662.text: A steady flow of an ideal fluid occurs through a horizontal pipe of varying cross-section. The kinetic energy per unit volume of the fluid at section A is $4$ times the kinetic energy per unit volume at section B. The ratio of the diameter of the pipe at section A to the diameter at section B ($d_A : d_B$) is:
101662.sol:
Kinetic energy per unit volume is given by $K = \dfrac{1}{2} \rho v^2$.

Given that $K_A = 4 K_B$, we have:
$\dfrac{1}{2} \rho v_A^2 = 4 \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \rho v_B^2 \right)$
$v_A^2 = 4 v_B^2 \Rightarrow v_A = 2 v_B$

According to the equation of continuity, $A_A v_A = A_B v_B$.
Since the cross-sectional area $A = \dfrac{\pi d^2}{4}$, we can write:
$d_A^2 v_A = d_B^2 v_B$
$\left( \dfrac{d_A}{d_B} \right)^2 = \dfrac{v_B}{v_A} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Taking the square root on both sides, we get:
$\dfrac{d_A}{d_B} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Thus, the ratio $d_A : d_B$ is $1 : \sqrt{2}$.

Answer: $1 : \sqrt{2}$

103668.subject: Physics
103668.text:
Match List I with List II for a circular current-carrying coil of radius $R$, where $x$ is the distance from the centre on its axis and $B_c$ is the magnetic field at the centre.

List I (Distance $x$)List II (Magnetic Field $B$)
(A) $x = 0$(I) $\dfrac{B_c}{8}$
(B) $x = R$(II) $B_c$
(C) $x = \sqrt{3}R$(III) $\dfrac{B_c}{27}$
(D) $x = 2\sqrt{2}R$(IV) $\dfrac{B_c}{2\sqrt{2}}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
103668.sol:
The magnetic field on the axis of a circular coil of radius $R$ at a distance $x$ from the centre is given by:
$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$

The magnetic field at the centre ($x = 0$) is $B_c = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$.
Thus, the ratio is $\dfrac{B}{B_c} = \left(\dfrac{R^2}{R^2 + x^2}\right)^{3/2}$.

(A) For $x = 0$: $B = B_c$
(B) For $x = R$: $\dfrac{B}{B_c} = \left(\dfrac{R^2}{2R^2}\right)^{3/2} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \Rightarrow B = \dfrac{B_c}{2\sqrt{2}}$
(C) For $x = \sqrt{3}R$: $\dfrac{B}{B_c} = \left(\dfrac{R^2}{R^2 + 3R^2}\right)^{3/2} = \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{3/2} = \dfrac{1}{8} \Rightarrow B = \dfrac{B_c}{8}$
(D) For $x = 2\sqrt{2}R$: $\dfrac{B}{B_c} = \left(\dfrac{R^2}{R^2 + 8R^2}\right)^{3/2} = \left(\dfrac{1}{9}\right)^{3/2} = \dfrac{1}{27} \Rightarrow B = \dfrac{B_c}{27}$

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)

104126.text:
An AC source of $200 \text{ V}$ (rms) is connected across a series LCR circuit. The rms current in the circuit is observed to be $4 \text{ A}$, and the voltage leads the current by a phase angle of $53^{\circ}$. If the capacitive reactance of the circuit is $10 \Omega$, what are the values of the resistance and the inductive reactance, respectively?
(Take $\cos 53^{\circ} = \dfrac{3}{5}$)
104126.sol:
The impedance of the circuit is given by:
$Z = \dfrac{V_{\text{rms}}}{I_{\text{rms}}} = \dfrac{200}{4} = 50 \Omega$

From the impedance triangle, the resistance $R$ is:
$R = Z \cos \phi = 50 \times \cos 53^{\circ} = 50 \times \dfrac{3}{5} = 30 \Omega$

Since the voltage leads the current, the circuit is inductive ($X_L > X_C$). The net reactance is:
$X_L - X_C = Z \sin \phi = 50 \times \sin 53^{\circ} = 50 \times \dfrac{4}{5} = 40 \Omega$

Given that the capacitive reactance $X_C = 10 \Omega$:
$X_L - 10 = 40 \Rightarrow X_L = 50 \Omega$

Thus, the resistance is $30 \Omega$ and the inductive reactance is $50 \Omega$.

Answer: $30 \Omega$ and $50 \Omega$

$\begin{aligned} & \text{  As } V_R=V_L=V_C \\ & \mathrm{R}=X_L=X_{C,} \Rightarrow Z=R \\ & V=I R=10 \text{ volt }\end{aligned}$
When capacitor is short circuited,
$Z=\sqrt{R^2+X_L^2}=\sqrt{R^2+R^2}=R \sqrt{2}$
New current $I^{\prime}=V / Z=V / R \sqrt{2}=\frac{10}{R \sqrt{2}}$
Potential drop across inductance
$=I^{\prime} X_L=I^{\prime} R=\frac{10 \times R}{R \sqrt{2}}=\frac{10}{\sqrt{2}}$ volt

105237.subject: Physics
105237.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When a p-n junction is reverse biased, the magnitude of the electric field in the depletion region increases, but its direction remains the same as in the unbiased state.

Reason (R): In a reverse-biased p-n junction, the applied external electric field is directed from the p-side to the n-side, opposing the built-in electric field.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
105237.sol:
The built-in electric field in a p-n junction is directed from the n-side (positive donor ions) to the p-side (negative acceptor ions).

In reverse bias, the positive terminal of the external battery is connected to the n-side and the negative terminal to the p-side. This creates an applied external electric field that is also directed from the n-side to the p-side.

Since the external electric field and the built-in electric field are in the same direction, they add up. This increases the overall magnitude of the electric field in the depletion region while its direction remains unchanged (from n to p). Thus, Assertion (A) is correct.

Reason (R) states that the external electric field is directed from the p-side to the n-side and opposes the built-in field, which is incorrect. Therefore, Reason (R) is false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect

106855.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
106855.text:
Consider the following two statements
$Statement I:$ Among $\mathrm{Mg}, \mathrm{Al}, \mathrm{Mg}^{2+}, \mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ the one having smallest size is $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$
$Statement II:$ Eu is having exceptionally high atomic radii among lanthanide elements
The correct answer is
options: Both statements I and II are correct
Both statements I and II are not correct
Statement I is correct but statement II not correct
Statement I is not correct but statement II is correct
106855.sol:
$\mathrm{Al}$ atom is smaller than $\mathrm{Mg}$ atom as $\mathrm{Al}$ lies to the right of $\mathrm{Mg}$ and it has greater effective nuclear charge. A cation is smaller than its parent atom so $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ is smaller than $\mathrm{Al}$ and therefore $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ is smallest in size.
Thus, statement I is correct.
Among lanthanides there is a gradual decrease in the atomic and ionic radii as we move from left to right due to lanthanoid contraction.
As per the latest data from rsc.org; the atomic radii of Sm, Eu and Gd are:-
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{Sm}=236 \mathrm{pm}, 185 \mathrm{pm} \text{ (covalent) } \\
& \mathrm{Eu}=235 \mathrm{pm}, 183 \mathrm{pm} \text{ (covalent) } \\
& \mathrm{Gd}=234 \mathrm{pm}, 182 \mathrm{pm} \text{ (covalent) }
\end{aligned}$
Thus, the radii of lanthanides decreases gradually with europium following the same trend.
Thus, statement II is false.

106880.subject: Chemistry
106880.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
106880.text:
Which of the following are correct?
(i) First ionisation enthalpy of $\mathrm{He} < $ Second ionization enthalpy of Li.
(ii) Li has the highest second ionisation enthalpy.
(iii) All $d$-block elements are transition elements.
(iv) The only alphabet not found in the periodic table is the letter ' $\mathrm{J}$ '.
(v) Francium concentration is $\sim 10^{-18} \mathrm{ppm}$ on Earth.
106880.sol:
All transition elements are $d$-block elements but all $d$-block elements are not transition metals. A transition metal is one which forms one or more stable ions which have incomplete $d$-orbitals. On the basis of this definition, scandium and zinc do not count as transition metal although they are d-block elements.
Thus, statement (3) is incorrect.

109396.text: An aqueous solution of ammonium hydroxide is taken in a conical flask and titrated against standard hydrochloric acid from a burette. Which of the following is the most suitable indicator for this titration and what is the colour change observed at the end point?
109396.sol:
Ammonium hydroxide ($\mathrm{NH_4OH}$) is a weak base and hydrochloric acid ($\mathrm{HCl}$) is a strong acid. The salt formed at the equivalence point is ammonium chloride ($\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$), which undergoes cationic hydrolysis to give an acidic solution ($\mathrm{pH} < 7$).

For a strong acid-weak base titration, methyl orange is the suitable indicator. Since the indicator is added to the weak base in the conical flask, its initial colour in the basic medium is yellow. At the end point, the addition of a slight excess of strong acid changes the medium to acidic, turning the indicator red.

Answer: Methyl orange, yellow to red

114441.text:
Given,
(i) $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}+2 \mathrm{e}^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$,
$\mathrm{E}^{\circ}=0.337 \mathrm{~V}$
(ii) $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}+\mathrm{e}^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{+}$,
$\mathrm{E}^{\circ}=0.153 \mathrm{~V}$
Electrode potential, $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ for the reaction, $\mathrm{Cu}+\mathrm{e}^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$, will be
114441.sol:
Key Idea Gibb's free energy is an additive property.
$$
\Delta \mathrm{G}^{\circ}=-\mathrm{nFE}^{\circ}
$$
For reaction, $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}+2 \mathrm{e}^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$;
$$
\Delta G^{\circ}=-2 \times \mathrm{F} \times 0.337
$$
For reaction, $\mathrm{Cu}^{+} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}+\mathrm{e}^{-}$;
$$
\Delta \mathrm{G}^{\circ}=+1 \times \mathrm{F} \times 0.153
$$
Adding Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$$
\begin{gathered}
\mathrm{Cu}^{+}+\mathrm{e}^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu} ; \quad \Delta \mathrm{G}^{\circ}=-0.521 \\
\quad \Delta \mathrm{G}^{\circ}=-\mathrm{nFE}^{\circ} \\
-0.521 \mathrm{~F}=-\mathrm{nFE}^{\circ} \\
\therefore \quad \mathrm{E}^{\circ}=0.52 \mathrm{~V}
\end{gathered}
$$

116365.subject: Chemistry
116365.text:
Match List I with List II.

List IList II
(A) $\mathrm{N_2}$ molecule(I) Single bonds only
(B) $\mathrm{P_4}$ molecule(II) $\mathrm{p\pi-p\pi}$ multiple bonding
(C) $\mathrm{R_3P=O}$ molecule(III) $\mathrm{d\pi-p\pi}$ multiple bonding
(D) Transition metal complex with $\mathrm{PEt_3}$(IV) $\mathrm{d\pi-d\pi}$ backbonding

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
116365.sol:
Nitrogen ($\mathrm{N}$) is a small atom and forms strong $\mathrm{p\pi-p\pi}$ multiple bonds with itself, resulting in the $\mathrm{N \equiv N}$ triple bond in the $\mathrm{N_2}$ molecule. (A matches II)

Phosphorus ($\mathrm{P}$) is larger and does not effectively form $\mathrm{p\pi-p\pi}$ bonds. Instead, it undergoes catenation through $\mathrm{P-P}$ single bonds, forming the tetrahedral $\mathrm{P_4}$ molecule. (B matches I)

In $\mathrm{R_3P=O}$, phosphorus uses its vacant $\mathrm{3d}$ orbital to overlap with the $\mathrm{2p}$ orbital of oxygen, forming a $\mathrm{d\pi-p\pi}$ double bond. (C matches III)

Heavier elements like phosphorus and arsenic can act as ligands (e.g., $\mathrm{PEt_3}$, $\mathrm{AsPh_3}$) and accept electron density from the filled $\mathrm{d}$-orbitals of transition metals into their own empty $\mathrm{d}$-orbitals, forming $\mathrm{d\pi-d\pi}$ backbonds. (D matches IV)

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

117816.subject: Chemistry
117816.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): $[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br$ and $[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4$ are ionisation isomers and the coordination number of cobalt in both complexes is 6.

Reason (R): Ionisation isomerism occurs when the counter ion in a complex salt is itself a potential ligand and can displace a ligand which can then become the counter ion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
117816.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: The complexes $[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br$ and $[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4$ yield different ions in solution ($Br^-$ and $SO_4^{2-}$ respectively), hence they are ionisation isomers. In both complexes, the central cobalt ion is bonded to 6 donor atoms (5 from $NH_3$ and 1 from $SO_4^{2-}$ or $Br^-$), making the coordination number 6.

Reason (R) is true: This is the exact definition of ionisation isomerism as per NCERT. The counter ion ($Br^-$ or $SO_4^{2-}$) acts as a potential ligand and displaces a ligand from the coordination sphere.

Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A) because it provides the underlying principle for why the given pair of complexes exhibit ionisation isomerism.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

121013.subject: Chemistry
121013.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During the curdling of milk by lactic acid bacteria, the primary structure of the milk proteins remains intact.
Reason (R): The change in $\mathrm{pH}$ during curdling causes unfolding of globules and uncoiling of helices, leading to loss of biological activity.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
121013.sol:
Curdling of milk is a common example of denaturation of proteins caused by a change in $\mathrm{pH}$ due to the formation of lactic acid.

During denaturation, secondary and tertiary structures of proteins are destroyed because the hydrogen bonds are disturbed, causing globules to unfold and helices to uncoil. This leads to the loss of biological activity. Thus, Reason (R) is true.

However, the primary structure, which consists of amino acids linked by strong covalent peptide bonds, remains intact during denaturation. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.

While both statements are factually correct, Reason (R) describes what happens to the higher-order structures (secondary/tertiary) and the resulting loss of activity. It does not explain why the primary structure remains intact (which is due to the stability of peptide bonds against mild $\mathrm{pH}$ changes). Therefore, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

123998.text: Which of the following are found in plant cells but not in animal cells?

124729.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cells situated just proximal to the meristematic zone in a root tip exhibit increased vacuolation and new cell wall deposition.
Reason (R): These cells possess primary, thin, and cellulosic cell walls with abundant plasmodesmatal connections.

124729.sol:
The cells situated just proximal to the meristematic zone represent the phase of elongation. According to NCERT, these cells are characterised by increased vacuolation, cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition. Therefore, the Assertion (A) is true.

The characteristics mentioned in the Reason (R) — primary, thin, and cellulosic cell walls with abundant plasmodesmatal connections — belong to the cells in the meristematic phase, not the elongation phase. Therefore, the Reason (R) is false.

Hence, Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

Assertion: Glucose is the favoured respiratory substrate.
Reason : When glucose is used as respiratory substrate it is completely oxidised and RQ is 1 .
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
125199.sol:
The ratio of the volume of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ evolved to the volume of $\mathrm{O}_2$ consumed in respiration is called the respiratory quotient (RQ) or respiratory ratio.
$\mathrm{RQ}=\frac{\text{ Volume of } \mathrm{CO}_2 \text{ evolved }}{\text{ Volume of } \mathrm{O}_2 \text{ consumed }}$
The respiratory quotient depends upon the type of respiratory substrate used during respiration. When carbohydrates are used as substrate and are completely oxidised, the RQ will be 1 , because equal amounts of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and $\mathrm{O}_2$ are evolved and consumed respectively.
$\begin{gathered}\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}_6+6 \mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 6 \mathrm{CO}_2+6 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\text{ Energy } \\ \mathrm{RQ}=\frac{6 \mathrm{CO}_2}{6 \mathrm{O}_2}=1\end{gathered}$

125421.subject: Botany
125421.text: Which pathway is associated with a 3-carbon acid as the first product?
125421.sol: Let us now ask ourselves a question that was asked by the scientists who were struggling to understand the ‘dark reaction’. How many carbon atoms would a molecule have which after accepting (fixing) CO2 , would have 3 carbons (of PGA)? The studies very unexpectedly showed that the acceptor molecule was a 5-carbon ketose sugar – ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP). Did any of you think of this possibility? Do not worry;Scientists also tried to know whether all plants have PGA as the first product of CO2 fixation, or whether any other product was formed in other plants. Experiments conducted over a wide range of plants led to the discovery of another group of plants, where the first stable product of CO2 fixation was again an organic acid, but one which had 4 carbon atoms in it. This acid was identified to be oxaloacetic acid or OAA. Since then CO2 assimilation during photosynthesis was said to be of two main types: those plants in which the first product of CO2 fixation is a C3 acid (PGA), i.e., the C3 pathway, and those in which the first product was a C4 acid (OAA), i.e., the C4 pathway.
125421.meta: Which pathway is associated with a 3-carbon acid as the first product?

125781.subject: Botany
125781.text: What is the structure of the anther described as?
125781.sol: the two parts of a typical stamen – the long and slender stalk called the filament, and the terminal generally bilobed structure called the anther. The proximal end of the filament is attached to the thalamus or the petal of the flower. The number and length of stamens are variable in flowers of different species. If you were to collect a stamen each from ten flowers (each from different species) and arrange them on a slide, you would be able to appreciate the large variation in size seen in nature. Careful observation of each stamen under a dissecting microscope and making neat diagrams would elucidate the range in shape and attachment of anthers in different flowers. A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed with each lobe having two theca, i.e., they are dithecous Often a longitudinal groove runs lengthwise separating the theca.

125809.subject: Botany
125809.text: What is the ploidy of the cells of the microspore tetrad?
125809.sol: As each cell of the sporogenous tissue is capable of giving rise to a microspore tetrad. Each one is a potential pollen or microspore mother cell. The process of formation of microspores from a pollen mother cell (PMC) through meiosis is called microsporogenesis. The microspores, as they are formed, are arranged in a cluster of four cells–the microspore tetrad As the anthers mature and dehydrate, the microspores dissociate from each other and develop into pollen grains Inside each microsporangium several thousands of microspores or pollen grains are formed that are released with the dehiscence of anther. Pollen grain: The pollen grains represent the male gametophytes. If you touch the opened anthers of Hibiscus or any other flower you would find deposition of yellowish powdery pollen grains on your fingers.

125948.subject: Botany
125948.text: How does endosperm persist in seeds like castor and coconut?
options: It is consumed before seed maturation
It is used up during seed germination
125948.sol: Endosperm development precedes embryo development. Why? The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly and forms a triploid endosperm tissue. The number of free nuclei formed before cellularisation varies greatly. The coconut water from tender coconut that you are familiar with, is nothing but free-nuclear endosperm (made up of thousands of nuclei) and the surrounding white kernel is the cellular endosperm. Endosperm may either be completely consumed by the developing embryo (e.g., pea, groundnut, beans) before seed maturation or it may persist in the mature seed (e.g. castor and coconut) and be used up during seed germination. 127775.subject: Botany
127775.text:
Read the following statements regarding the process of decomposition:

A. Humus is highly resistant to microbial action and undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate.
B. The degradation of humus by microbes to release inorganic nutrients is called humification.
C. Water-soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon during leaching.
D. Bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances by the process of fragmentation.

Which of the above statements are correct?
127775.sol:
Statement A is correct: Humus is a dark-coloured amorphous substance that is highly resistant to microbial action and decomposes extremely slowly.

Statement B is incorrect: The degradation of humus by microbes to release inorganic nutrients is called mineralisation, not humification. Humification refers to the accumulation of humus.

Statement C is correct: During leaching, water-soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts.

Statement D is incorrect: The degradation of detritus into simpler inorganic substances by bacterial and fungal enzymes is called catabolism, whereas fragmentation is the physical breakdown of detritus by detritivores.

Therefore, only statements A and C are correct.

Answer: A and C only

127805.subject: Botany
127805.text:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Gross primary productivity(I) Rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers
(B) Net primary productivity(II) Available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs
(C) Secondary productivity(III) Rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis
(D) Respiratory loss(IV) Difference between gross primary productivity and net primary productivity

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
127805.sol:
Gross primary productivity (GPP) of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. Therefore, (A) matches with (III).

Net primary productivity (NPP) is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers). Therefore, (B) matches with (II).

Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers. Therefore, (C) matches with (I).

Respiratory loss (R) is the difference between gross primary productivity and net primary productivity (GPP - NPP = R). Therefore, (D) matches with (IV).

Hence, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)

Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults especially in middle age can result in severe disfigurement (especially of the face) called Acromegaly, which may lead to serious complications, and premature death if unchecked. The disease is hard to diagnose in the early stages and often goes undetected for many years, until changes in external features become noticeable. Prolactin regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them. TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland. ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of steroid hormones called glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex. LH and FSH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called gonadotrophins. In males, LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of hormones called androgens from testis. In males, FSH and androgens regulate spermatogenesis. 128339.subject: Zoology
128339.text: What are the hormones commonly known as?
128339.sol: The adrenal medulla secretes two hormones called adrenaline or epinephrine and noradrenaline or norepinephrine. These are commonly called as catecholamines. Adrenaline and noradrenaline are rapidly secreted in response to stress of any kind and during emergency situations and are called emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight. These hormones increase alertness, pupilary dilation, piloerection (raising of hairs), sweating etc. Both the hormones increase the heart beat, the strength of heart contraction and the rate of respiration.Glucocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis; and inhibit cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids. Cortisol is also involved in maintaining the cardio-vascular system as well as the kidney functions. Glucocorticoids, particularly cortisol, produces anti-inflammatory reactions and suppresses the immune response. Cortisol stimulates the RBC production. Aldosterone acts mainly at the renal tubules and stimulates the reabsorption of Na+ and water and excretion of K+ and phosphate ions. Thus, aldosterone helps in the maintenance of electrolytes, body fluid volume, osmotic pressure and blood pressure.Small amounts of androgenic steroids are also secreted by the adrenal cortex which play a role in the growth of axial hair, pubic hair and facial hair during puberty.
